pr_title: drivers/uart: stm32: Fix TC flag handling in IRQ driven mode
pr_body:
When modifying driver to use PM constraints to handle PM requests,
some change of behavior was introduced in IRQ driven mode,
to accommodate with the new usage of _TC flag.

This had impact in some scenarios, like shell for instance.
Likely, TC flag was cleared too soon, having consequences on
behavior on functions were it is checked (irq_is_pending,
irq_tx_complete).

Fix this by clearing the flag on fifo_fill.

EDIT:
~~Additionally, remove code enabling IT on driver init,
as this doesn't work well with some platforms (F4).~~ > Fixed by the following:

EDIT: Additionally, in polling mode take into account byte streams (Fixes #38620)

Tested on:
- nucleo_wb55rg (shell, uart_basic_api, pm, shell + pm)
- nucleo_f429zi (shell, uart_basic_api, uart_async_api)

Fixes #38519

Signed-off-by: Erwan Gouriou <erwan.gouriou@linaro.org>

EDIT: Also fixes:
- tests/drivers/uart/uart_async_api/drivers.uart.uart_async_api disco_l475_iot1

issue_context.title: stm32: g0b1re: Log/Shell subsys with serial uart buggy after #38432
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
The log and shell subsys is acting strangely (sluggish and buggy) after the merge of #38432. Most notably, the shell responds only after second keystrokes. For example if `a` is pressed, nothing appears on the screen. Pressing `a` again will have two `a`s on the shell.

I'm seeing this on my G0B1RE custom board, reverting #38432 solves the issue.

**To Reproduce**
I've tried the `hello_world` with `CONFIG_SHELL` enabled on the `nucleo_g0b1re`, same issue as my custom board

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Win10
 - Toolchain: GNUARMEMB
 - f83dc928f6

**Logs**
```
I: Starting bootloader
I: Primary image: magic=good, swap_type=0x1, copy_done=0x3, image_ok=0x1
I: Scratch: magic=unset, swap_type=0x1, copy_done=0x3, image_ok=0x3
I: Boot source: primary slot
I: Swap type: none
I: Bootloader chainload address offset: 0x10000
I: Jumping to the first image slot
***** delaying boot 2000ms (per build configuration) *****





uild time: Sep 15 2021 16:52:30 Malaysia!





1: Turn on modem

32m[00:00:04.011,000] <inf> hw_manager: Starting modem
gmoc:~ $
```

review_comments: I've done some quick tests, seems that by just removing this line the shell works as before. It probably requires some more investigation, the IRQ API is really low-level so we've probably missed something.

Removing this line solve the shell issue on some board indeed.
Though, it at least requires to be moved elsewhere (otherwise uart_stm32_irq_tx_complete is always true.)

Anyway, doing all this makes things worst on others boards, as nucleo_f429zi cannot output chars anymore.
It seems that on such target, TC flag is always asserted (which might also require some investigation)
